title: Tech firms pledge $2.4B in computing power to Trump’s Genesis Mission
source_used: Nextgov/FCW (same story as the Politico item)
key_facts: At the White House AI Science Summit on Thursday 8 Oct 2026, 11 tech companies pledged $2.4 billion in compute credits for the Genesis Mission Consortium.
Pledges: Nvidia $1 billion, AMD $500 million, OpenAI $200 million, Anthropic and Google $150 million each; others $100 million or $50 million.
The credits are to support over 15 federal agencies working on national science and technology challenges.
The administration billed the summit as a $6 billion push for US-led science and technology.
The Pentagon announced up to $350 million for quantum computing initiatives; the Energy Department announced $159 million in Phase II awards and $96 million for early-career researchers.
Trump also awarded national technology and science medals to six tech executives, including Elon Musk.
quote_evidence: Eleven tech giants pledged to provide $2.4 billion in compute credits for the Genesis Mission Consortium, which the White House said will be used to support “over 15 Federal agencies working towards National Science & Technology Challenges.”
The industry commitments included $1 billion from Nvidia, $500 million from AMD and $200 million from OpenAI.
why_it_matters_hint: Federal scientists are promised large amounts of computing power for AI research, paid for by industry credits rather than public money.
notes: Politico page returned 403; same story read at Nextgov/FCW, which wrote its own reporting. Politico headline matches. Related to C04-03 (Energy Department awards, same summit).
